steps.what: Open the filled prescription and applicable price record
Resolve price and reimbursement exceptions within delegated limits
Compare prescription references with dispensing and archive records
Verify final price and prescription filing reference
Commit the priced prescription filing

tasks.design: Configure a filled-prescription view in the pharmacy-system category of {OTHER}, linking price, dispensing and archive references. Native identifier checks replace repeated cross-screen comparisons; the technician resolves exceptions and verifies the final filing before committing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate price, dispensing and archive screens require repeated reference comparisons.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked views and exact identifier checks can show discrepancies together.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear coverage and mismatched prescription identities require investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a price that is technically valid but inappropriate for the prescription context.
tasks.altitude: Less cross-screen comparison; pharmacist escalation rules do not change.

reach.learn: Reimbursement rules and archive audit trails

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10 for pharmacy access and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: pharmacy records can link prescription, dispensing and price identifiers for deterministic consistency checks.

assumptions: Boundary: post-dispensing price confirmation and filing of electronic prescriptions. Dispensing, clinical checks and insurer submission are separate. Paper scanning is not assumed.

Upstream dispensing supplies prescription_id, patient_id, product_id, quantity, dispensed_at and archive_reference; authorised billing staff maintain price, effective_date and reimbursement_code. Missing or conflicting references remain manual in s2/s3.

Test native views and validation first. s3 savings are the exact ID/price comparisons now performed across screens, not a general reduction in clinical review. Existing price calculation and archiving runtime earn no labour saving.
s5 is a near-zero native commit represented by the required minimum 1% and fully retained. Gross 22%; focal upkeep 1 gives net 21%. Shares are provisional, not observed baselines or prior-derived.
unknowns: Whether reference comparison is already automatic
research_questions: Can the linked view detect wrong-patient and stale-price references without hiding exceptions?

approvals.approved_version: approved prescription filing v1 with patient, prescription, final price and archive reference; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% if native matching already covers the work and no change is made; 18% if missing archive references retain three more baseline hours than central net 21%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count, order and label stock and maintain inventory records.

steps.what: Count physical stock and identify lots and expiry dates
Enter observed quantities and lot details in inventory
Prepare replenishment quantities against approved stock limits
Verify counts and approve the final replenishment order
Commit the approved inventory count
Send the approved stock order to the supplier
Label current stock and verify labels against actual lots
Save verified label-batch details in inventory

tasks.design: Configure the pharmacy inventory module in {OTHER} with a product-linked count form and reorder proposal from approved stock limits. Retain counting, scanning, lot verification and label application; submit only the exact approved order through the existing supplier connection to {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated product entry and manually assembled reorder quantities.
tasks.enabler_now: Native product selection, reorder rules and supplier order interfaces may already exist.
tasks.still_hard: Expired lots, shortages, controlled items and misleading on-hand quantities.
tasks.human_edge: Check physical stock rather than relying on an expected balance.

ambition.what: Review near-expiry replenishment exceptions at each count cycle.

tasks.altitude: Less order assembly; stock safety and purchase limits remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Pack units, supplier acknowledgements and delegated limits

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10 for supplier credentials and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: product-linked forms and deterministic reorder rules can assist pharmacy stock ordering without replacing physical counts.

assumptions: Boundary includes current-stock count, count record, routine replenishment order and labels on current stock. Receipt of a future delivery is a later cycle, not assumed before it arrives.

s1 produces product_id, lot_id, expiry_date, counted_quantity and count_time; s2 captures them manually. Authorised stock owners already maintain reorder_min, target_max, pack_size, supplier_id and price_limit; open orders come from existing purchasing. Missing rules keep manual proposals in s3.

Native count/reorder/supplier settings are tested first. s2 retains scanner operation and all quantity capture; savings are product/lot field reuse. s3 retains proposal checking; s4 retains final quantity and authority review. Orders outside delegated limits are excluded and escalated unchanged.
s5/s8 are near-zero same-system saves, minimum 1% each fully retained. s6 is a real separate supplier send. Gross saving 18.5%; upkeep 1.5 gives net 17%.
unknowns: Supplier connection and delegated order limits
research_questions: Do proposals account for open orders and pack sizes without substituting unapproved products?

already_counted.description: Verify count and approve final order

incremental.description: Report stale stock rules and check supplier mappings

approvals.approved_version: approved stock packet v1 final observed counts; changed counts void approval
approved stock packet v1 exact supplier, products, packs and amounts; any change voids approval
approved label record v1 with verified products and lots; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% with already-configured inventory and no change; 14% when missing pack rules and supplier mismatches retain three extra baseline hours versus central net 17%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compute and record patient medication or equipment charges.

steps.what: Retrieve the dispensed items for the patient episode
Select effective tariff and equipment charging rules
Enter quantities and tariff codes to form charge lines
Investigate returns, unit mismatches and missing tariff codes
Verify patient, quantity, tariff and final total
Post approved charges to the patient account

tasks.design: Configure episode-linked charge entry in the pharmacy or patient-billing category of {OTHER}, with effective-date tariff selection and reuse of recorded dispensed quantities. The technician reviews the proposed codes and quantities, resolves exceptions and approves posting; no model is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dispensing and charge-entry screens can require repeated item and quantity selection.
tasks.enabler_now: Native charge mappings can populate draft lines from the selected episode.
tasks.still_hard: Returns, reusable equipment rules and missing mappings require investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Spot a charge inconsistent with what was actually dispensed.
tasks.altitude: Less charge-line entry; no new tariff-setting authority.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10 for billing permissions and national consultation where applicable

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: effective-date rules and product mappings can populate charge drafts deterministically.

assumptions: Boundary: technician preparation and posting of hospital patient charge lines, excluding clinical dispensing and invoice collection.

Existing dispensing staff supply patient_id, episode_id, product_id, quantity, unit, dispensed_at and returns. Billing staff already maintain tariff_code, price, effective_dates and unit conversion. Missing mappings or unit uncertainty retain manual work in s4; no proposed quantity substitutes for actual use.
Test native charge-entry configuration first. Existing arithmetic runtime is not human work and earns no saving; s2/s3 reductions are repeated code selection and re-entry only.
s6 is a near-zero native post represented by 1%, fully retained. Gross 27%; upkeep 0.8 gives central net 26.2%.
unknowns: Who owns tariff mapping and exception handling
research_questions: Can repeated charges be prevented with dispensing-event identifiers?

incremental.description: Report mapping failures and sample charge-line fidelity

approvals.approved_version: approved patient charges v1 final patient episode, quantities, codes and totals; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% when charge lines already populate without technician re-entry and no change is installed; 22% when unmatched equipment and return lines retain 4.2 extra baseline hours versus central net 26.2%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and process medical insurance claims and records.

steps.what: Gather filled prescription and coverage details for the claim
Complete payer claim fields and supporting references
Resolve missing eligibility, coding and supporting-document exceptions
Verify the final claim and approve payer submission
Save the approved claim record
Submit the approved claim to the insurer
Inspect the transmission receipt and identify submission failures

tasks.design: Use native claim-field mappings and payer validation in the pharmacy-system category of {OTHER}. The technician resolves exceptions and approves the exact claim before a configured connection sends it to {PARTNER_PORTAL}; a separate human step checks the transmission receipt.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated payer field entry and separate submission screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured payer formats and native claim connections can reuse pharmacy records.
tasks.still_hard: Eligibility disputes and missing support are not solved by formatting a claim.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a rejection needs factual correction rather than repeated resubmission.
tasks.altitude: Less claim typing; coding and eligibility decisions remain within delegated limits.

reach.learn: Payer error codes and correction controls

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-12 for payer credentials and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: structured insurer claims can be mapped and validated deterministically, while eligibility exceptions need human resolution.

assumptions: Boundary: prepare, retain and submit the claim, including receipt checking. Adjudication is insurer work and unchanged, outside the focal denominator; later appeals are not assumed eliminated.

Dispensing supplies prescription_id, product, quantity and service_date. Existing insurance records supply patient_id, policy_id and insurer_id; authorised billing staff supply payer field rules. s1 gathers these; missing eligibility is manually resolved in s3 using an existing coverage response or manual payer lookup.
Test native claims configuration first. No invented narrative extraction or automated eligibility decision. s5 is a near-zero same-system save, minimum 1% fully retained.
s6 is a separate real send; s7 retains all receipt-checking time. Gross saving 21%; focal upkeep 1.5 gives central net 19.5%.
unknowns: Who may approve and submit claims
research_questions: Does the configured connector stop duplicates after a timeout?

already_counted.description: Check submission receipt and transmission failures

incremental.description: Maintain payer mappings and audit rejected claims

approvals.approved_version: approved claim v1 final payload and supporting references; edits void approval
approved claim v1 exact payload, attachments and insurer destination; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% for an already-integrated claim flow with no deployment; 16% if payer exceptions retain 3.5 extra baseline hours versus central net 19.5%.

reach: Support purchasing clerks with checked replenishment orders
Support billing clerks with reliable claim corrections
role.ambitious_version: A technician who can maintain reliable stock and billing records without trading away physical verification or pharmacist escalation.
